panels.title: Worker heartbeat
panels.description: Seconds since the leader last beat. The API calls execution unavailable at 30s -- three missed beats. 86400 means no worker has ever run.

panels.title: Worker holds leadership
panels.description: 1 when a worker_state row exists at all.

panels.title: Execution available
panels.description: The leader is execution-enabled and no order is in recovery. This is the same bit users see.

panels.title: Orders needing recovery
panels.description: A single one halts its strategy and blocks new automatic admission for everyone.

panels.title: API serving traffic
panels.description: GET /ready's own verdict. A missing worker never affects it.

panels.title: Order activity, 15-minute window
panels.description: Orders that changed status in the last fifteen minutes. This is the submission-failure signal: the lifetime census below cannot tell forty reverts over six months from forty in five minutes.

panels.title: Open orders
panels.description: admitted = reserved against the signed envelope, nothing signed. pending = at least one leg in flight. Both are meant to be transient.

panels.title: Oldest open order
panels.description: Funding expires 60s after admission, so anything past ~900s is holding a budget reservation that will never be spent.

panels.title: Oldest unreceipted transaction, by leg
panels.description: A signed transaction with no receipt. A stuck fund leg has pulled nothing; a stuck swap leg has the user's USDC sitting in the spender wallet. The worker itself stops waiting at 1800s.

panels.title: Unreceipted transactions, by leg
panels.description: Count of journal rows still in `signed`.

panels.title: Journal census
panels.description: Every journalled transaction by leg and status. The journal is immutable and is the record of what was signed.

panels.title: Order census
panels.description: Lifetime orders by status and stage.

panels.title: Schedule lag
panels.description: How far behind the worst armed instance is. The maximum, not the mean: one starved strategy is an incident that an average over a thousand healthy ones hides. Missed evaluations are never replayed.

panels.title: Armed and overdue instances
panels.description: Overdue is measured only over armed instances: a paused one keeps whatever due time it had and would dominate forever.

panels.title: Evaluation outcomes, 15-minute window
panels.description: `evaluated` is the healthy one. deferred/late/degraded are the scheduler describing itself, not failures.

panels.title: Evaluation failure ratio
panels.description: Share of evaluations that did not evaluate, excluding the scheduler's own bookkeeping rows. Backoff means a persistently failing instance contributes fewer rows, so a sustained quarter can only be a shared dependency.

panels.title: Strategy population
panels.description: Instances by lifecycle status and mode.

panels.title: Reference age by symbol
panels.description: THE panel for feed staleness. The dashed lines are 72h (one heartbeat of margin left) and 96h (MAX_VALIDATION_AGE -- past it nothing can be quoted). A weekend legitimately puts every symbol at 37-43h; that is not a fault.

panels.title: Oldest reference
panels.description: max(mandate:reference_age_seconds:max). NaN ages -- feeds that could not be read at all -- are excluded, because one NaN would poison the maximum.

panels.title: Feeds readable
panels.description: Symbols for which a Chainlink round was read at all, regardless of age. A drop here is an RPC or aggregator fault, not staleness.

panels.title: Symbols the API calls stale
panels.description: The 26h display bound. DIAGNOSTIC ONLY -- every symbol sits here for the whole of every weekend by design, and nothing alerts on it.

panels.title: Quote deviation from reference
panels.description: Signed bps between the probe price and the Chainlink reference. The router refuses at +/-500; the measured healthy figure for AAPLc/USDC is about 4 bps.

panels.title: Catalogue coverage
panels.description: Five of the seven listed equities route on Base today; MSFTc and AMZNc do not, on ~$150k pools. So the healthy tradable count is 5, not 7. `dropped` is entries this exporter refused.

panels.title: Why an asset is not tradable
panels.description: One row per (symbol, reason) currently set. Every reason is exported for every symbol, so an empty table means everything routes -- not that the query is broken.

panels.title: Tradable, by symbol
panels.description: 1 when the small exact-input probe cleared the reference band.

panels.title: Routed tick spacing
panels.description: Which Slipstream pool the best quote came from. AAPLc/USDC prices correctly at spacing 10 and 11,729% out at 200, so a change here means liquidity moved to a pool nobody has looked at. Deliberately not alerted on: the deviation panel above is what catches the consequence.

panels.title: API probe error ratio
panels.description: Share of probes not returning the answer the route is defined to give. A 503 from /ready scores ok: refusing traffic is that endpoint's job.

panels.title: Probe traffic
panels.description: Requests this exporter issues, and the ones that came back wrong.

panels.title: Probe latency
panels.description: Wall time of the most recent probe of each route. /v1/market composes an oracle read and a quoter probe per asset, so it is legitimately the slow one.

panels.title: Database ready
panels.description: Reachable, migrated, and NOT reached through a superuser or BYPASSRLS role.

panels.title: Chain ready
panels.description: The Base RPC answers and reports chain id 8453.

panels.title: Execution available (as the API reports it)
panels.description: The API's view, which requires a heartbeat under 30s old. The database gauge beside it is the raw stored flag with no freshness test, so after a stopped worker the two legitimately disagree -- that difference is the useful part.

panels.title: Market collection succeeding
panels.description: 1 when the last GET /v1/market returned a usable catalogue.

panels.title: Scrape targets down
panels.description: Every rule that reads a down target has stopped evaluating, and silence from a rule looks exactly like health.

panels.title: Collection freshness
panels.description: All three in seconds. `last success` climbing means the per-symbol gauges above are frozen; `snapshot age` should oscillate inside the API's 15s cache and a monotonic climb means its refresh is wedged.
